page: Vultr vcg-a40-6c-30g-12vram is a Cloud GPU server instance featuring a fractional NVIDIA A40 GPU based on the Ampere architecture. This configuration provides 0.25 of a physical A40 GPU, delivering 12 GB of dedicated VRAM. The host system is powered by an Intel x86_64 processor, allocating 6 shared vCPUs and 30.0 GB of system memory, which equates to 5.0 GB of RAM per virtual core.

Local storage is bundled with the instance, consisting of a 550 GB NVMe SSD to support high-throughput local read and write operations. The instance also includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Because the CPU allocation is shared, CPU-bound performance may vary depending on host node utilization, making this instance more suitable for workloads that offload primary computation to the GPU.

By partitioning the NVIDIA A40 GPU into a 0.25 fractional slice, this instance offers a cost-efficient entry point for workloads that require GPU acceleration but do not need a full dedicated GPU. This resource density is appropriate for small-scale machine learning inference, model prototyping, video transcoding, and moderately demanding CUDA-accelerated data processing tasks.
